#

Today marks the 10-year anniversary of DACA — the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals program.
Before I talk about where we go from here, I want to acknowledge that DACA was created in the first place because of the voices, the activism, and the relentless organizing of immigrants.
And for these past 10 years, along with the benefits and protections that DACA has provided for Dreamers, there has also been deep uncertainty.
As a Senator from California (home to more immigrants and specifically more Dreamers than any other state), and as the son of two immigrants from Mexico myself, I understand the urgency of the fight to reform our broken immigration system.
Because the truth is, immigrants deserve better. Dreamers deserve better. America is better than this, and that’s why we are not giving up.
Dreamers are our teachers, our doctors, our nurses, our frontline workers in so many sectors that have been so critical during this pandemic. They deserve better than to live in uncertainty or fear of changing immigration status or deportation.
That is why we’re going to keep up the fight for permanent protections and a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers, and then build on that success to fix our broken immigration system.
We’re going to explore any path forward. If Republicans are not going to come along, we must do everything in our power — including eliminating the filibuster — to get it done.
And in the meantime, we’ll keep pressing President Biden to use his executive authority to build on DACA and protect more Dreamers.
Thank you,
\- Alex Padilla

* * *

**Alex Padilla is the son of immigrants from Mexico, and the first Latino to represent California in the U.S. Senate. Now, he’s on the front lines of the fight to protect our democracy, reform our broken immigration system, and protect our environment for future generations.**

Dear Peter,

This week, South Central Montana experienced devastating floods and the rivers are still high. At yesterday's public briefing for the residents of Red Lodge, Penny learned that four bridges were lost within two hours in Red Lodge alone. Through videos and news reports, we've all seen the devastation from Yellowstone National Park to Red Lodge, East Rosebud to Fromberg, Roscoe to Billings, and more.

We have also seen the power of community.

People helping people and caring for one another.

name: Team AOC
subject: This is ambitious
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Last quarter, they raised $665k. We believe they could raise even more this quarter. This is money that will be funneled into attack ads, negative mailers, and brazen lies about AOC and our campaign. But you can help us fight back.
# [](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/143?refcode=em20220615-3107-header&t=1&akid=3107%2E2526796%2EZ_SMrg)
With the primary election in just 70 days, our race’s landscape is rapidly changing. Redistricting added new communities to our district, forcing us to quickly scale our organizing efforts to reach every new constituent and voter.
**Plus we officially have 5 Republicans and Conservatives hoping to go up against us in the general election.** And they’re raising — FAST. So far, our Republican opponents have raised $665,000 in just Q1 alone.
As we approach the end of our second fundraising quarter, we don’t know what those numbers will look like when they’re reported in July. We believe they could raise even more this quarter. This is money that will be funneled into attack ads, negative mailers, and brazen lies about AOC and our movement. But you can help us fight back.
[We’ve set an ambitious goal in response. We want to make sure we at least MATCH what our Republican opponents raised last quarter. Can you help us reach $665,000 this quarter to keep AOC in Congress?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20220615.eW2UW4&refcode=em20220615-3107-P_FND_EOQ_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=3107%2E2526796%2EZ_SMrg)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20220615.eW2UW4&refcode=em20220615-3107-P_FND_EOQ_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=21&akid=3107%2E2526796%2EZ_SMrg)**
Here’s the logic: Keeping AOC focused on the issues in Congress is critically important. We want her fighting for a Green New Deal, not batting down brazen lies by Republicans on the campaign trail.
If we can match what these opponents have raised last quarter, then we’ll be ready to defend ourselves against whatever they throw our way. Then, we can keep AOC fighting for progressive legislation on Capitol Hill and helping elect progressive allies across the country.
[You can make a big difference today, even if it’s only by donating a few dollars. Will you help us match what our opponents raised, and reelect AOC?](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20220615.eW2UW4&refcode=em20220615-3107-P_FND_EOQ_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=22&akid=3107%2E2526796%2EZ_SMrg)
**[Contribute $3](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-20220615.eW2UW4&refcode=em20220615-3107-P_FND_EOQ_GFM&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=23&akid=3107%2E2526796%2EZ_SMrg)**
In solidarity,
Team AOC

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/aoc-email-20220615?refcode=em20220615-3107-P_FND_EOQ_GFM&t=24&refcode2=3107_2526796_Z_SMrg&akid=3107%2E2526796%2EZ_SMrg)** | **[Merch](https://shop.ocasiocortez.com/?utm_source=em-footer-20220615-3107-P_FND_EOQ_GFM&t=25&akid=3107%2E2526796%2EZ_SMrg)**

clean_body: | | | Friend, We know that you’re a strong supporter of Republicans, which is why we couldn’t pass up the opportunity to send you this message. Nikki Haley is taking the stage TOMORROW. She’s dedicated to defeating Democrats and taking back the House and Senate majorities, and we know you are too, friend, so we need your help today. We know it would mean the world to Nikki to know you’re on our side as we train, endorse, advise, and financially support strong conservative candidates so we can win back our Republican majorities in 2022. Thank you. Sincerely, Stand For America PAC | A Note From Nikki: Growing up, smart, strong, and unconventional women were discouraged. When I ran for office, the South Carolina legislature was dominated by a Good Old Boys' Club and my opponent thought women shouldn’t be in politics. People thought I was too brown, too female, too young, too conservative, too principled. I said: Too bad. I was inspired by great women who broke barriers and defied expectations, women like Margaret Thatcher and Jeane Kirkpatrick. That’s why I wrote this book.
